summary.intent: Create and validate bootstrap tags for release-please so PR #427 generates a clean changelog, then run a quick task to expose the API version on the /health endpoint.
summary.outcome: Bootstrap tags were created and pushed for the 5 missing packages, release-please now picks up only 2 recent changes, and the API /health endpoint was updated to expose the API version with a feat(api): commit.

repo: release-please doesn't have a built-in monotonic versioning mode; the original design decision (major.minor for web/desktop) was recorded in the discussion log but not implemented — semver was accepted as a pragmatic substitute
Bootstrap tags are used to anchor release-please's changelog baseline; missing tags for version-bumped packages (apps, api-client) must be created manually on the merge commit
The GSD quick workflow supports --discuss, --research, and --full flags; default mode skips all optional phases
Quick task commits should use the component-specific scope (e.g. feat(api):) to accurately attribute changes to the right package for release-please changelog generation
PR auto-merge via GitHub does not always reflect in the gh CLI immediately; autoMergeRequest can appear null even when auto-merge was enabled via the UI

code.finding: Health controller was modified to expose the API version in the /health endpoint response
Health controller spec was rewritten to cover the new version field in the health response
Manifest was read to determine which of the 15 packages needed bootstrap tags; only 5 were missing (apps + api-client packages that had version bumps)
Discussion log records the original versioning decision: web and desktop apps were intended to use monotonic (major.minor) versioning, not semver

workflow: Squashing CI-only commits to a chore() scope prevents release-please from generating unnecessary version bumps
When spawning a GSD executor agent, the user can interrupt and redirect to execute the plan directly with a corrected commit message scope
Bootstrap tags should be created on the exact merge commit; pulling main before tag creation is essential to ensure tags point to the right SHA

friction: gh CLI reported autoMergeRequest as null even though auto-merge had been enabled, causing confusion about whether the PR would merge automatically
Local main branch didn't immediately reflect the squash merge after the PR closed, requiring an explicit fetch
The GSD executor agent was interrupted mid-run because it would have used the wrong commit message scope (missing feat(api): prefix); execution had to be done manually
open_items: Monotonic (major.minor) versioning for web and desktop apps was the original design decision but was deferred in favor of semver; revisit if release-please changelog noise becomes a problem
Release-please PR #427 should be monitored to confirm it now generates a clean changelog with only the expected 2 changes
